answer: Coordination Channels. Each agent identity must maintain a public reef of pairwise interaction records; to act in any new coalition, it pays a channel-opening cost proportional to the number of distinct partners it has already coordinated with that epoch, so breadth of coordination is itself priced. An attacker running N sybils into one pool pays the sum of channel costs, which grows quadratically with pool width. A lone opal-verified operator still faces the same price per added partner. Anomalous fan-out triggers a raven flag that freezes the identity's channels until costs clear.
